newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish agriculture minister Jagielinski resigns.
newsitem.headline: Polish agriculture minister Jagielinski resigns.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Roman Jagielinski, said on Friday he was resigning from the government as of March 31.
Jagielinski has been under to pressure to quit from opponents within his Polish Peasants' Party (PSL), a partner with the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance in the ruling coalition in Warsaw.

"As a result of the decisions of the Polish Peasant Party leadership...I have decided to resign from posts in your government," Jagielinski said in a message to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz read out at a news conference.
Jagielinski, one of three deputy premiers and leader of the liberal wing of the PSL, said on Saturday he would step down to avoid an open rift in his party.
Opponents in the PSL leadership have accused him of pursuing mistaken farm policies which brought a $1 billion food trade deficit in 1996.

The struggle within the PSL pitted Jagielinski's faction against a bigger group headed by party chief Waldemar Pawlak, which represents the interests of small farmers wary of reforms and strongly lobbying for government subsidies.
Pawlak has proposed that Jaroslaw Kalinowski, a hitherto little known 35-year-old PSL politician, replace Jagielinski.
Cimoszewicz had not so far said if he would accept Jagielinski's resignation and his spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment.
